name: Brown Planthopper
description: A sap-sucking insect pest of rice that causes direct damage through feeding and indirect damage by transmitting viral diseases (rice ragged stunt virus, rice grassy stunt virus). Heavy infestations cause "hopper burn" — rice fields turning brown as plants die.
symptoms: Orange-brown insects at base of rice stems
Honeydew production supporting sooty mold growth
Plants turning yellow, then brown, beginning in circular patches
Hopper burn: large areas of dead, brown plants
Wilting and plant death in severe infestations
treatments: Apply systemic insecticides (imidacloprid, thiamethoxam) at early infestation
Use neem oil and insecticidal soap for light infestations
Drain fields partially to reduce planthopper habitat
Avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural enemies
prevention: Plant resistant rice varieties (carrying BPH resistance genes)
Use balanced nitrogen fertilization — avoid excess
Avoid dense planting to improve air circulation
Practice intermittent irrigation rather than continuous flooding
Monitor weekly during tillering to flowering stages
references: Africa Rice Center Integrated Pest Management
